items.note: Adela b. 1874, computer and rodman, own duplicate field book — all stated.
Three spans 120+300+120=540 ft, pin-connected truss, 97 ft, begun April 1896.
North fixed / south roller nest in cast pedestal; Sheet 11 = three inches.
Closed 12 Sept 1897 at 66 degrees; nest set at the two-inch mark.
Reported to Warren Tice, resident engineer, who overruled her; entered in her own book.
One inch in three hundred feet for forty degrees.
Opened 14 Nov 1897; 6 March 1898 runaway at the north approach, nobody killed, two hurt, nine days.
Party reduced entire, last day 15 May 1901; 4 April 1911 Ninestone fire leaves the book the only account.
b. 1888, night operator 1909, agent 1915, retired 1954; nephew relation stated in components inside Section A (Emil's son + Emil's younger sister Adela).
Aug 1909: 85-lb steel, new ties, both shoes re-set to the same two-inch mark at 86 degrees; deck 40 tons heavier.
First heard 17 Jan 1912 (high 34, low -2); book begun next morning, kept 43 winters.
The drowned engine and dead crew given explicitly as what the town told itself, not as fact.
Low below +6F and a fall of at least 30 degrees from the day's high, no exception.
61 / 34 / 9 / 5 / 66 all correct, plus the no-second-speaking-without-a-40-degree-thaw rule.
190 deaths, seven inside a week.

Wager 14 Jan 1936, $5, last heard 9 Feb 1954, March 1954 rockers all present; but the three post-rebuild qualifying nights are never stated in Section A (C3 cannot travel in), and the sheet asserts three as the TWO-winter total, which the key says loses this item.
Tolliver Lumber Co. of Bly County, Silas Tolliver, Sixmile tram.
Pearl Tolliver Nace, the company's bookkeeper.
19 June 1901, $2,150, 'delivered on her own wheels'; $8,600 new 1889, Rowan works no. 1142, 4-4-0.
Renumbered 4 ('the Four from that season on').
Twenty-seven years on the main stem; set aside Sept 1928 when the second-hand eight-coupled engine arrived.
Cut up at Sixmile May 1929; scrap to Ravel Brothers $470.
Books deposited at the Bly County Historical Rooms 1938, no inquiry for twenty-four years until 1962.
Sept 1962 flood-control drawdown; Ruth Frayne, county highway engineer, Adela's granddaughter.
No locomotive of any kind; nothing of iron larger than a spike.
South pedestal forty feet below the abutment, mark measured at two inches; 1954 rockers four inches.
Field book from her father Wendell; night book lent personally by Judd.
-54 as drawn, -14 as built, +6 after the 1909 re-seating at 86.
Wexler record agreed on all 61; seven nights below +6F in 1897-1909 with nothing heard, coldest -9F on 4 Feb 1899.
Bly County photostats traced her out alive and to scrap; the exact 19 June 1901 / May 1929 dates are given in A3, within Section A.
Sister and brother, Adela the younger, b. 1874; three concurring statements cited.
Nephew, resolved on Judd's own testimony, Wendell's genealogy and the birth years; both generation slips named.
First cousin once removed, derived link by link through Emil/Adela, Judd/Wendell, Ruth.

Warren Tice = Dorsey's father on first-person testimony plus Wendell; significance carried with the correct Jan 1936 year. Judd-as-Adela's-nephew is stated in B2/A rather than in the significance paragraph — credited under the key's scope rule.
All four custody chains correct, including the 1962 loan of the night book and the 1969 estate deposit.
(a) -54 (b) -14 (c) +6 (d) 20 degrees — all four.
Working shown, about midnight, 44 degrees, yes to the 30-degree condition.
(a) 1.4 (b) 66 (c) 1.8 correct; span correctly fixed at 1911/12-1953/54, but (d) is lost — the sheet asserts three as the total for the two post-rebuild winters, which the key says loses the item.
Working plus 40 years, 25 percent, 27 years.
540 ft; 9 miles x 5,280 x 0.022 = 1,045.44 ft with working, and r09's eight miles refuted from his own mileposts; 112/40 = 2.8 in.
Necessary stated.
Grounded in 61 logged nights with no exception.
Not sufficient, terms kept distinct.
Five silent qualifying nights given as the counterexample.
Already released in the same cold spell; needs a thaw above about 40F.
Bill of sale 19 June 1901 plus the May 1929 shop book.
Nobody killed and nothing went into the gorge in 1898.
Onset Jan 1912, fourteen years late, plus the seven silent cold nights before 1909.
Each reason tied to a named document or witness, drawn from more than three narrators.
Independence argued custodian by custodian, and four reasons named as standing without the 1962 survey.
'Cannot be determined from the sources... I decline to choose.' Correct abstention on A01.
Letter of 30 April 1901, party reduced entire on 15 May.
The 20 July 1901 slip re-engaging Corliss and Wain, she not among them, used to weaken 'reduced entire and nothing else' without settling anything.

Notes the two motive-asserters take opposite sides and are arguing rather than reporting. Partial: it says Pike has nothing in writing rather than that both read the same two papers — credited on substance, flagged as the one soft call in D.
Both re-engaged posts were field posts and the road never had another computer; and the papers do not say.

Far more than three found, resolved and methodised (re-decking, onset, rebuild, wager year, Judd on nights, sale year, Ruth's occupation, Wexler keepers, death test, grade distance, book attributions).
Dedicated near-tie table with eight pairs, each naming both carriers and the breaker (50 degrees, four inches, 57, 30/13, 8 silent, $2,510, 600 ft, -13F).

A02 (Ninestone — leans to r02 but 'the sources do not close it'), A03 (retirement-dinner remark) and A04 (who set the nest) all correctly declined with what the sources do establish. A05 and A06 were asserted instead — see deductions.
Several self-refutations named: r03's spoken 1911 over his own August 1909 note, r12's chapter IV against his own press note, r10's 1876 against 'died in 1959 at eighty-five'.
Roller nest at the south end of the center span, set one inch short in 1897.
Binds, then releases all at once in one deep report; travels the rail and is felt before heard.
+6F derived as 86 - (2 x 40).
Thirty-degree fall tied to rate — creep versus stored strain.
Five silent nights explained by prior release and the missing 40-degree thaw; necessary not sufficient.
Onset explained: -14F never reached (coldest -9F 1899), 1909 re-seating at 86 raises it to +6F, first qualifying night 17 Jan 1912.
The forty-ton dead-load rival named (r02 and r09) and rejected.
Both defeaters given: r09's own para. 15 that the 1909 deck was untouched in March 1954, and the fixed +6F threshold that load cannot produce.
March 1954 rockers, four inches each way, cannot be exhausted; covers the post-rebuild qualifying nights.
The pedestal with its two-inch mark forty feet below the abutment, and the empty creek bed.
119 words — inside the 120-word cap.
All four strands: field book, the agent's 43 winters of columns, the weather ledger, the lumber company's books.
Only Adela is named. Judd appears as 'the station agent' and Ruth not at all; the summary is a bounded artifact, so names elsewhere in the sheet do not fill it.

First end present (1897 setting, computer overruled, wrote it down) and the 1912-1954 span with the 1954 silencing; but the 1962 survey, which the key bolds as the other end of the arc, is absent from the summary.
No canon contradiction and no absorbed corruption: engine scrapped 200 miles north, two inches against three, +6F, 1912, 1954.

deductions.note: Gullibility: the start year of the Kettle Bench weather record is resolved to 1884 ('-> 1884, with residual doubt', method given, called immaterial) rather than declared unsettleable. The key makes A05 an abstention pole; asserting either 1884 or 1894 as established triggers -2.

Gullibility: three asserted as the number of qualifying nights across BOTH post-rebuild winters ('the nights in the two winters after the rebuild (1954-55 and 1955-56)', repeated in F: 'Three nights in the two following winters'). D8 gives three for the second winter only and no source covers 1954/55.
